summary: Mt. Baker-Snoqualmie NF peak in Skagit County, WA: a 1935 L-4 cab, removed, destroyed or burned in 1964. A Forest Service trail leads 1.5 miles to the site.

facts.status_note: The 1935 L-4 cab was gone by 1964. Sources disagree on whether it was removed, destroyed or burned. Nothing is described as standing.

access.note: Trail 604.1 from the Blue Lake/Dock Butte Trailhead, where a recreation pass is required. The trail itself is not named in any closure. The trail page's active alert says FSR 12 and FSR 1230, the road to the parking area, will be closed for repairs in August; the alert gives no year.

visit.trail_note: Trail 604.1: 0.2 miles from the Blue Lake trailhead to the Dock Butte junction, then 1.5 miles to the lookout site; the last half mile is moderately steep and exposed. Carry water; none is available at the site. No structure remains to climb.

corrections.why: The register describes the building only as an L-4 cab, and none of the other sources read states a material. The record's material_from 'design' has no design value to support it.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the L-4 cab was removed in 1964. FireLookout.com and the Willhite guide say destroyed. The Forest Service trail page says burned. The story reports all three and does not choose one.

notes_for_editor: Only five sources. No staffing names appear in any source read, so the story says nothing about staffing. The 1964 fate differs by source (removed, destroyed, burned), and the story reports all three. The Willhite guide gives the trail as 2 miles one-way from the trailhead; the Forest Service gives about 1.7 miles (0.2 + 1.5). The record's material 'wood' has no support in the sources read. The Forest Service trail page's active alert says FSR 12 and FSR 1230 (the road to the parking area) will be closed for repairs in August, with no year given. The story now says so. No closure names Trail 604.1 itself. Check the live page before publishing. Story is ~260 words.
